description: The model-execution kill switch and the provider-secret reference. This file decides whether a real provider call may happen at all. It is deliberately separate from `runtimeReady` in config/agent-roles.json: that flag says a role has been proven, this switch says the factory is currently permitted to spend money on a model. A proven role with the switch off makes no calls, and the switch being on promotes nothing.
rules: Default off until a reviewed repository change opts into a deliberate canary. `enabled: true` here is only the repository's answer; it is not a runtime toggle and authorises nothing without every independent prerequisite.

Two keys, both required. This file AND the host switch at `hostSwitchPath` must independently say enabled. Either one saying otherwise refuses every new model attempt, so an operator can stop the lane on the host without waiting for a merge, and a merge cannot start the lane on a host that has not opted in.

The switch is read on the trusted side and re-read immediately before every provider call. It is never an environment variable inside a sandbox, never a prompt instruction, and never something a task can observe or influence.

A credential is a reference here, never a value. `providerSecret.secretRef` names where the trusted gateway looks; the gateway resolves it in its own process and the value reaches no config, no ledger, no context packet and no sandbox.

Enabling the switch authorises nothing by itself. A model attempt additionally needs a signed, single-use enable decision naming the role, task, project, model and ceilings — see `npm run runtime:model-canary -- --authorise`.

Turning the switch off stops new provider calls immediately, and the canary supervisor cancels an attempt that is in flight. Anything already returned by the provider is still accounted for and recorded.

provider.modelReason: The smallest capable model for the first canary. A review verdict against named deterministic criteria does not need the largest model, and a cheap model makes the hard budget genuinely small rather than nominally small.

providerSecret.resolvedBy: the trusted model gateway process only

pricingGbpPerMillionTokens.note: Declared here so a response can be priced from its own token counts. The gateway refuses to record a call it cannot price, because an unpriced call is a budget nobody enforced. Overstating the rate is the safe direction: it makes the ceiling bind sooner.

canaryBudget.reason: One call, one verdict, five pence. Deliberately too small for anything but the canary: a budget that could fund a second task is a budget that would not have been noticed if the lane misbehaved.

canary.roleReason: The safest useful role in the registry for a first real attempt: network profile `none`, no mutation scope, no secret access, a projected capability set that is entirely reads, a typed output with a real JSON Schema (schemas/review-verdict.schema.json), and an existing reviewer rule that forbids it promoting its own work. It is already the reader role in the deterministic runtime canary, so its refusal set is covered by tests that exist.
